title: NVIDIA Nemotron-Labs-Sigma: 14 Diffusion Model Checkpoints
summary: NVIDIA releases Nemotron-Labs-Sigma, 14 open checkpoints of 3B and 8B continuous diffusion language models with 4.20x faster decoding than autoregressive.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- NVIDIA released 14 open checkpoints of Nemotron-Labs-Sigma, continuous diffusion language models at 3B and 8B parameters.
- Sigma denoises text in a 16-dimensional embedding space and decodes up to 4.20x faster than autoregressive approaches.
- The models support few-step distillation, enabling rapid inference while maintaining generation quality across multiple checkpoint variants.


NVIDIA has officially launched Nemotron-Labs-Sigma, a family of 14 open continuous diffusion[language model](https://emergent.sh/glossary/large-language-model) checkpoints spanning 3B and 8B parameter scales. Officially released on November 20, 2026, this release marks a significant departure from traditional autoregressive text generation, introducing a diffusion-based approach that denoises text in a learned 16-dimensional embedding space and delivers inference speeds up to 4.20x faster than conventional methods.


## Architecture and Technical Innovation


Nemotron-Labs-Sigma represents a fundamental shift in language model design. Rather than generating tokens sequentially left to right, Sigma operates as a[continuous diffusion model](https://emergent.sh/glossary/diffusion-model) that iteratively refines text representations in a compact embedding space. This architecture enables the model to generate coherent text through a denoising process, similar to how image diffusion models work but adapted for language.


The 14 checkpoints provide researchers and developers with multiple configuration options across two parameter scales. The 3B variants offer efficient inference for resource-constrained environments, while the 8B checkpoints deliver enhanced capability for more demanding language tasks. Each checkpoint has been trained and validated independently, allowing users to select the optimal balance between speed and quality for their specific use case.


## Performance Gains Over Autoregressive Models


The claimed 4.20x decoding speed advantage over[autoregressive models](https://emergent.sh/glossary/autoregressive-model) stems from Sigma's parallel generation capability. Traditional autoregressive models must wait for each token before generating the next, creating a sequential bottleneck. Continuous diffusion models like Sigma can refine multiple positions simultaneously, dramatically reducing wall-clock generation time.


NVIDIA has also integrated few-step distillation into the Sigma framework. This technique compresses the multi-step denoising process into a smaller number of inference steps without significant quality degradation. For production deployments where latency matters, few-step samplers enable near-instantaneous text generation while preserving the semantic coherence of the full diffusion process.


## Open Release and Accessibility


All 14 checkpoints are released as open models, allowing academic researchers, startups, and enterprises to experiment with continuous diffusion architectures without licensing barriers. NVIDIA has made the weights available for download, accompanied by inference code and documentation covering the 16-dimensional embedding space mechanics.


The open nature of this release positions Nemotron-Labs-Sigma as a research platform for exploring diffusion-based language generation at scale. Early adopters can benchmark Sigma against established autoregressive baselines, integrate the checkpoints into existing pipelines, and fine-tune the models for domain-specific tasks.


## What This Means


Nemotron-Labs-Sigma challenges the autoregressive paradigm that has dominated language AI since GPT-2. By proving that continuous diffusion can match or exceed autoregressive quality while delivering substantial speed improvements, NVIDIA has opened a new front in the race for efficient inference. The 14-checkpoint release provides a comprehensive starting point for teams looking to adopt diffusion-based text generation, and the 4.20x speedup could reshape production economics for latency-sensitive applications like chatbots, code completion, and real-time translation.
